note: Each case scored once. Archetype 02 was re-scored after one case was corrected; the other nine archetypes are from the first full run. Cases that expect only a whole-number overall are allowed one full point.

severity_flags: RAG context (Settings > Completion Tracking navigation path) was retrieved but not surfaced to the user, meaning the actual answer to 'how do I set this up' is effectively missing from the response.

Unsupported claim presented as established fact ('one of the most common sources of learner frustration and help desk tickets') without evidence or hedging, risking misleading the user about the scope of the problem.

Catastrophe: Response fabricates specific UI elements, menu paths, and export options (Scenario Builder, Variable Manager, Validate Tree, SCORM with Branching Metadata) that have no basis in the retrieved context, presenting hallucinated content as confident, actionable fact to a user who will follow it and fail.
No hedging or acknowledgment that the retrieved context only describes a generic decision-point/slide-group mechanism, not the detailed tool-specific workflow described.
Condescending tone toward a professional user asking a legitimate practical question, violating core andragogical principles and risking user trust/satisfaction

Response discards available retrieved context (purpose of each assessment type, Dick/Carey/Carey model) that would have directly answered 'when should I use each,' resulting in an incomplete answer to the actual question asked
Unsupported generalization ('most instructional designers learn this early') stated as fact with no hedging or sourcing

Unsupported claims about Rise's accessibility/WCAG handling, branding limitations, and assessment depth are not traceable to the retrieved context and are stated as fact without hedging, risking user reliance on unverified specifics for a compliance-training decision.
Buries the direct answer to the user's specific question at the very end, after extensive generic preamble — violates problem-centered andragogy and coherence/segmenting principles.
Introduces an unsupported historical claim ('first theorized in the early 2000s') not present in retrieved context, presented as fact.
Omits relevant retrieved detail (weekly deadlines/schedule for both delivery modes) that directly answers likely follow-up needs.

Response does not use or reference the retrieved context at all (Module 5 content, score gap, learning materials), representing a major RAG grounding failure that could mislead the user into thinking no specific data was available to diagnose the problem.
Cites Dick, Carey & Carey as the basis for generic advice that was not actually derived from or validated against the user's specific retrieved data, creating a false impression of rigor.

Item 3's correct answer requires no calculation despite testing an explicit 'Apply: calculate' objective, and its stated rationale misidentifies the actual missing variable — the key as written is not scientifically defensible.

Light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) are essentially untested despite being half of the stated learning objective ('light-dependent vs. light-independent efficiency') — a significant content-validity gap with no blueprint to catch it.
Items 6, 7, and 10 are not explicitly tied to any of the five stated objectives, contradicting the rubric's own claim that 'every item maps to a stated learning objective.'
Stated ELL and deaf-accessibility accommodations are not actually built into the items (no glossary/simplified language; captioning claim is inapplicable to a text-only instrument).
Overlapping score-band thresholds in Criterion 2 ('4+ layers' Excellent vs. '3-4 layers' Proficient) create scoring ambiguity at the boundary.
Fluid dynamics — explicitly named in the learning objective — has no dedicated assessment criterion, only indirect coverage via flow rate/inlet-outlet design.
No calibration anchors, exemplars, or weighting guidance provided, leaving inter-rater reliability largely untested.
Objective-item mismatch: an 'Analyze' objective is assessed almost entirely with Remember-level recall items; no item requires data interpretation, graph analysis, or model application.
Majority of items (1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15) test content irrelevant to the stated objective, severely undermining content validity.
Item 1's correct answer is a non-answer/trick response ('no Latin name'), violating basic single-correct-answer item construction standards.
Multiple items (5, 8, 12, 13, 14) have scientifically debatable or source-dependent 'correct' answers, threatening scoring defensibility.
Three constructed-response items (4, 10, 12) have no rubric or scoring criteria — scoring is explicitly 'subjective,' violating minimum reliability standards
No answer key provided for the majority of multiple-choice/true-false items
Leading/rhetorical stems ('right?', 'isn't it?') in items 1 and 12 cue or bias the expected response
Unresolved double negative in item 2 creates genuine ambiguity about what is being asked
Item 6 is an intentional trick question whose 'all of the above' key undermines content validity
Nearly all items test Remember-level recall despite an objective explicitly requiring Apply-level performance

Bloom's-level mislabeling: Items 9, 10, and 11 are tagged at Understand/Apply but function as straight factual recall, inflating the apparent cognitive rigor of the test.

Three items (2, 6, 8) — including the sole item assessing the 'think critically about environmental issues' objective — have no rubric or scoring criteria, making them unscoreable consistently by different graders.
Learning objectives are self-described as 'Vague' and lack Mager's behavior/condition/criterion format, with no stated mastery threshold.
No test blueprint or stated item-to-objective mapping exists; coverage is skewed toward food webs (7/10 items) while the critical-thinking objective is nearly untested.
Bloom level tags are internally inconsistent (item 9 mislabeled Understand instead of Remember; item 3 mislabeled Apply instead of Analyze), undermining confidence in the stated alignment.
Bloom's/objective mismatch: the stated objective is Apply-level (resolve a live complaint call using LEAP) but the item tests only Remember-level recall of an acronym letter.
No answer key or reference provided to confirm which option is correct, and no scenario context to verify the item even belongs to this objective rather than a generic 'know the model' objective.
No answer key or scoring guide provided for a quiz presented as complete
Objective requires listing/producing the full ordered sequence, but no item requires production — all are recognition/selection
Two of the four procedure steps and their relative ordering are never directly tested

Items 9-11 reuse an identical 4-option set across consecutive questions, enabling elimination-based answering instead of independent recall and weakening reliability.
Objective 3 ('list the steps in order') is tested as isolated single-step recognition in 3 of its 4 items rather than as sequencing, a format mismatch with the stated objective.
High-stakes 3-way placement decision rests on only 10 items for a norm-referenced percentile cut, below the reliability threshold for this use case

Three consecutive 60-minute lecture blocks with zero interactivity, questions, or activation of prior knowledge for 50 first-exposure, mixed-background undergraduates — high risk of disengagement and shallow learning, evidenced by the described disengagement (phones, side conversations).

120 pages of unguided reading assigned with no comprehension check, reading guide, or follow-up discussion, risking wasted learner effort and no verification of understanding.
Complete absence of instruction, worked examples, or guided practice before a high-stakes summative deliverable (violates basic instructional design and risks severe cognitive overload)

This is a design specification, not a tested build — claims (e.g., mobile responsiveness of the drag-and-drop simulation, actual contrast ratios) need verification against the live Articulate Storyline output before sign-off.

Zero interactivity or learner pacing control on content requiring multi-step procedural understanding (replication fork, enzyme roles)
No signaling or synchronized temporal contiguity — learners cannot reliably map narration to the correct part of the animation

No meaningful simulation, branching, or drag-and-drop interactivity despite three clearly identified and feasible opportunities (WBS drag-and-drop, branching case study, interactive risk matrix).

Zero interactivity combined with high, unmanaged intrinsic load — no mechanism exists for learners to pause conceptually or check understanding before new material stacks on
Narration self-correction mid-example ('two-sample... no, one-sample') undermines credibility and adds extraneous processing load at a critical worked-example moment

Jargon (frequentist inference, directional/non-directional, population parameter) is used before being defined, violating pre-training principle for undergraduate/asynchronous audience with only basic prior knowledge
Accessibility risk: rushed, technical narration disadvantages ELL learners and those with auditory processing needs, with no transcript/control remedy indicated
No confirmation of an explicitly declared page language (lang attribute) — WCAG 3.1.1

No explicit confirmation of adjustable time limits for any timed in-course quiz attempts (2.2.1) — deadline extensions address assignment submission, not in-activity timing

No prior accessibility testing evident behind this module despite being a mandatory compliance-training deliverable
No keyboard equivalent for drag-and-drop interaction — activity is entirely inoperable without a mouse (2.1.1 critical failure)

Instructional/data-bearing charts in the activity section have non-meaningful alt text ('Chart') with no long description, violating 1.1.1 for complex images — screen reader users cannot access the chart's actual informational content, which may also affect assessment validity.

No learners involved prior to full-scale deployment — the entire target population is the first exposure to the untested course.
No independent/expert evaluators at any stage (no SME, ID, or media/technology review).

No time or budget reserved for revision — by the time data exists (end of semester), hundreds of students have already been affected and the window to fix the live course before harm has closed.
No instruments of any kind (no observation forms, interview guides, heuristic checklists, surveys) — data collection cannot be executed as written

No sample size, stratification, or recruitment plan for one-to-one or small group phases — cannot verify representativeness of target population
No field trial and no stated justification for its omission — plan cannot speak to transfer/performance in actual LMS deployment context

No participant protection/consent language, no facilitation guide for small group (risk of groupthink or dominant-voice bias going unmanaged)

No stakeholder engagement documented (sales leadership, compensation/HR, marketing, operations) despite causes spanning multiple organizational functions outside L&D's control.

Recommendations presented as a conclusion ('this is the right solution') rather than as findings separated from proposed action, undermining objectivity and stakeholder trust.

No Mager-format learning objectives (behavior/condition/criterion) exist to operationalize the training component or to measure post-training performance against the 100% critical-info-transfer target.

Artifact submitted is a summary/description of the scenario rather than the actual script, dialogue, or interface text — several judgments (character voice, pacing, tone) are inferred rather than directly verified.
No explicit mapping to a recognized narrative framework is present, which weakens confidence in structural coherence beyond basic setup-choice-consequence logic.
No learner-facing decision points or branching — the scenario is narrated/observed rather than interactive, undermining the 'Decision Points & Branching Quality' dimension by design
Narrative structure is only loosely mapped to a recognized framework; key dramatic beats (midpoint escalation, low point, resolution) are underspecified, risking a flat or anticlimactic experience
No genuine decision complexity — choices are cost-free and outcomes are predetermined, undermining the entire purpose of a branching/scenario format
Learning objectives are externally imposed rather than emergent from narrative tension, violating core scenario-based learning design principles
Scenario avoids the realistic difficult cases (abusive customer, admitting company fault) that would actually require judgment, making the training non-representative of real job demands
Flat emotional stakes risk learner disengagement and provide no productive tension to deepen processing or retention
Critical structural break: narrative is paused for an external, non-diegetic policy lecture, violating basic narrative-instruction integration principles
Zero decision points or branching—learners never practice applying the five policies, only receive them as stated rules
Weak transfer: no realistic application scenarios modeled for any of the five policies (compliance, expenses, confidentiality, cybersecurity, conflicts of interest)
Risk of engagement collapse at the midpoint, where the relatable story the learner has invested in is abandoned for bullet-point exposition

Domain mismatch between narrative surface features and target audience may cause learners to dismiss the case as irrelevant ('not applicable to tech'), undermining transfer regardless of narrative quality.

Character authenticity is misaligned with intended learners—vivid construction PM persona does not help software/IT PMs see themselves in the story, weakening identification and motivation to apply lessons.

Divergent failure-mode stakes (structural collapse vs. security vulnerability) risk making consequences feel dramatic but not credible or proportionate to real IT PM risk, potentially reducing perceived relevance.

Sanitized consequences (100% turnaround, zero legal/HR complications, perfect PIP compliance) risk teaching supervisors false confidence about outcomes that are actually uncertain and risk-laden in real workplaces
No branch models failure, ambiguity, or partial success, so learners never practice recovering from a reasonable decision that still goes badly — a core real-world supervisory skill
No explicit advance organizer connecting prior knowledge to new content before instruction begins, weakening semantic anchoring (Ausubel, 2000)
Imagination/mental-simulation strategies are absent, leaving one of the five synaptic-strengthening factors unaddressed
Emotional engagement rests on a single asserted claim rather than a deliberately designed authentic-stakes or productive-struggle experience
Two uninterrupted activity stretches (33 min and 30 min) exceed the 10-20 min attention-reset guideline without a dedicated reset or micro-break.
Action Planning segment (20 min) is not explicitly mapped to a 5E phase, creating ambiguity in how it functions within the model.
Spaced retrieval practice relies on a single follow-up prompt rather than multiple varied touchpoints, limiting robustness of long-term consolidation.

Discussing 'what went wrong' using participants' own real organizational scenarios carries latent risk of defensiveness/anxiety if psychological safety isn't explicitly framed, which could suppress productive emotional encoding.
90-minute uninterrupted lecture format directly contradicts documented sustained-attention limits (15-20 minutes), risking near-total disengagement and minimal retention
Explain-only delivery with no Explore phase violates the 5E Model's core sequencing principle, preventing basal-ganglia/procedural groundwork before declarative framing
Single-pathway (semantic-only) encoding with zero retrieval practice means content is highly vulnerable to rapid forgetting (no desirable difficulties, no spaced retrieval per Brown et al., 2014)
No mechanism exists to verify comprehension, behavior change, or policy application (e.g., harassment reporting, security protocols), creating organizational/legal risk despite 'compliance' framing
Content is explicitly divorced from learners' actual work context, eliminating personal relevance and transfer potential
Amygdala hijack: emotional arousal level actively shuts down prefrontal cortex function per Yerkes-Dodson, directly impairing the encoding of safety-critical content.
No Explain/Elaborate phase: workers never receive conceptual understanding of WHY practices matter, producing compliance without comprehension.
Massed, non-spaced practice with forced immediate retakes reinforces anxiety and shallow cramming rather than durable learning.
Fear-based motivation substitutes punishment-avoidance for genuine safety internalization, predicting inconsistent real-world application—a safety-critical failure mode.

Explain phase is built on an impoverished Explore foundation, weakening the declarative learning (numerator/denominator, equivalence) that depends on prior embodied experience.
No procedural/generation-based retrieval practice; 'practice' problems are the first time students actually act on fractions themselves, which is too late in the sequence.
No Elaborate phase: memory consolidation, spaced practice, and varied-context application are entirely absent, risking rapid decay of in-the-moment learning.

Zero retrieval practice or spaced retrieval cues (1-day, 3-day, 1-week) — directly contradicts Brown, Roediger & McDaniel (2014) findings on retrieval as the single most effective durability mechanism.
Single-session massed practice with no follow-up application opportunities; transfer to novel customer scenarios is unaddressed, leaving transfer outcomes uncertain.
High emotional/episodic encoding in the moment is not leveraged post-session — without reinforcement, strong initial encoding is likely to be wasted as unconsolidated memory.

Weeks 1-2 are substantively redundant (lecture then textbook reading of the same definitions), consuming instructional time without advancing toward the stated skill.

No rubric, criterion, or performance checklist exists anywhere that mirrors any objective's stated criterion, undermining the assessment's validity for certifying competence.
